The `goalService(db)` returns an object of functions — no DB calls happen during construction. The `db` methods are only called when the returned functions are invoked. So the stub approach should work.

However, there's a subtlety: `expressHandler(listGoals, { db, storage: storageSentinel })` stores `deps.db` in a closure. When the handler is later called (by Express in prod, or by our bridge in CF), it would use the stub `db`. But in the CF Worker, we don't call the Express handler — we call the tagged `__handler` (the original `Handler` function), which uses `ctx.db` from the `RequestCtx` passed in at call time. The `deps.db` stored in the closure is never used via the bridge. Let me verify this by looking at how `listGoals` uses db:

Looking at `goalRoutes`: `listGoals` is `Handler = async (ctx) => { ... await svc.list(companyId) }`. The `svc` is `goalService(db)` where `db` is the stub. So when `listGoals(ctx)` is called, it calls `svc.list(companyId)` which calls `stubDb.select()...`. This will throw!

The issue is that the `Handler` captures `svc` which was built from `_stubDb`. I need a different approach.

Option A: Build real `db` objects per-route-factory call at request time (but this means moving route factory calls inside the fetch handler, which causes duplicate registration).

Option B: Don't use the stub-based route extraction at all. Instead, extract routes lazily (once per cold start, on first request).

Option C: Change the service pattern — instead of closing over `svc = goalService(stubDb)`, pass `db` through `ctx.db` and have the Handler use `ctx.db` directly rather than closing over `svc`.

Looking at the actual goal handler: the `listGoals` Handler closes over `svc` which was built from the factory's `db` arg. So the stub approach will fail at runtime.
